exposure: abnormal or indeterminate fetal heart rate
cohort: The study included 22,265 live births at an academic tertiary center between 2009 and 2013.
finding: The overall cesarean delivery rate decreased from 36.5% to 31.4% from 2009-2013, with primary cesarean births accounting for 74% of this decrease, largely driven by reductions in diagnoses of labor arrest (44%) and abnormal fetal heart rate (23%).
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate decreased significantly, primarily due to a reduction in primary cesarean deliveries stemming from fewer diagnoses of labor arrest and abnormal fetal heart rate.
